projects.functionalBrief: The proposed headquarters supports a single organization with a mix of focused work, team collaboration, client meetings and staff amenities. Employees and visitors arrive through a legible shaded reception sequence, while deliveries, facilities operations and building maintenance are handled separately from the principal pedestrian court.
programme: Enclosed team rooms and meeting rooms
Boardroom in the southwest corner volume
projects.floorOrSiteOrganization: Four low rectilinear office bars enclose a planted rectangular courtyard, with the single, modestly taller boardroom block at the southwest corner. A deep two-storey arcade links the shaded entry plaza, reception and court; work areas occupy the wings, with meeting and amenity rooms near the shared circulation. Keep a clear accessible visitor route from the street, a separate screened service approach to loading and plant, and protected stairs with direct discharge to open space at the required exit locations.
projects.areaOrScale: Proposal-stage allowance: approximately 8,000–10,000 m² gross internal area across three to four levels, including the taller boardroom portion; about 350–450 regular workplace users, subject to detailed occupancy and code review. Site allowance approximately 1.0–1.4 ha including arrival plaza, court, setbacks and service access.
projects.structuralSystem: A regular reinforced-concrete beam-and-column frame, provisionally on an approximately 7.5–8.5 m office bay, supports flat floor plates and the low office bars. Concrete cores and stair walls provide lateral stability; the two-storey arcade is carried on concrete columns and beams, with transfer elements only where verified by structural design. Boardroom spans may use deeper reinforced-concrete or steel beams to keep the principal room column-free.
projects.constructionLogic: Use a conventional concrete frame with locally sourced granite paving, board-formed concrete arcade soffits and non-loadbearing office infill. Terracotta baguettes are individually mechanically supported on a corrosion-resistant subframe fixed back to the primary structure, with movement joints and accessible glazing-cleaning zones. Roof build-up falls to concealed gutters and accessible rainwater outlets; planted roof zones require root-resistant waterproofing, protection layers, drainage and overflow routes. Build the frame and weather-tight roof first, then façade screens and landscape works, maintaining temporary drainage and safe separation of site logistics from the public arrival route.
projects.environmentalResponse: Set out the bars and openings to admit useful diffuse daylight while limiting direct low-angle sun; calibrate terracotta screen density by façade orientation and retain high-performance, limited glazing behind the shade. The deep arcade and planted court provide outdoor shade and moderated microclimate, while operable windows may support mixed-mode use when outdoor conditions and acoustics permit. Capture roof runoff for landscape irrigation, route overflow to planted infiltration areas where soil and groundwater conditions allow, and select native canopy planting for shade with manageable water demand.

projects.functionalBrief: The proposed mid-rise workplace provides adaptable, daylit floor plates for office teams, meeting and support functions. It prioritizes straightforward visitor arrival, secure staff circulation and discreet servicing, with façade shading intended to improve visual comfort without compromising useful views or maintenance access.
programme: Loading, waste holding and building management
projects.floorOrSiteOrganization: Arrange a compact mid-rise office block on a regular structural grid around a central service core containing lifts, toilets, risers and protected stairs. Place reception and a sheltered entrance on the public frontage; maintain clear, direct public access to the lobby and a separate back-of-house route from service access to waste, loading and plant. On upper floors, keep flexible work areas at the naturally lit perimeter and meeting/support rooms closer to the core. Provide separated protected escape routes and accessible discharge at grade in accordance with the applicable code.
projects.areaOrScale: Proposal-stage scale: approximately 6,000–8,000 m² gross floor area over six to eight levels, with typical office plates of roughly 800–1,000 m² and an indicative capacity of 350–500 people subject to final fit-out and life-safety calculations. Urban plot allowance approximately 0.25–0.4 ha including setbacks, arrival court and service access.
projects.structuralSystem: A reinforced-concrete flat-slab or beam-and-slab frame on a regular 8–9 m office grid is paired with a reinforced-concrete central core for lateral resistance. Slab edges support the curtain wall and separately bracketed limestone fins; fin dead loads and wind loads are carried by engineered stainless-steel or aluminium anchors back to the frame. Final grid, slab depth, foundations and movement provisions require geotechnical and structural engineering.
projects.constructionLogic: Construct the core and floor frame in a coordinated sequence, then install insulated glazing units and bronze-toned slab-edge covers with continuous perimeter fire-stopping. Limestone fins are segmented to manageable lengths and fixed to engineered brackets with isolators, drainage gaps and replaceable connections; provide access for inspection and façade cleaning. Coordinate sill, head and slab-edge flashings so water drains outward without trapping moisture behind the stone. Complete the sheltered entrance and accessible street interface early enough to coordinate utilities, while protecting the façade and public route during lifting and installation.
projects.environmentalResponse: Orient the longer office elevations to reduce east- and west-facing exposure where the site permits, and tune fin depth and spacing to the actual solar path rather than treating all façades identically. The external fins reduce glare and solar gain while retaining high-performance glazing and useful daylight; provide glare-controlled lighting and operable windows only where outdoor air, noise and building systems allow. Plant the forecourt and setbacks for shade, use efficient irrigation or captured runoff where feasible, and direct roof and podium drainage to maintainable outlets with safe overflow paths.

projects.functionalBrief: The proposed open-air retail quarter accommodates small and medium shops, food uses and informal gathering in a walkable, weather-protected setting. It must support accessible customer circulation, deliveries, waste collection and maintenance while remaining porous to breezes and managing intense coastal rainfall without depending on enclosed-mall operation.
programme: Food and beverage units with service back rooms
Plant, water storage and maintenance access
projects.floorOrSiteOrganization: Cluster compact rectangular pavilions around one central rain court beneath a single gently vaulted elevated canopy. Covered pedestrian lanes form a continuous accessible circulation loop with clear connections to the street, public transport and parking/drop-off as applicable; arrange shopfronts toward these routes and locate tenant back rooms toward a discreet service edge. Keep service vehicles outside principal pedestrian areas, with timed deliveries and screened waste holding. Provide multiple clearly legible open-air egress routes from the court and lanes to the site perimeter, with travel distances and fire separation verified for the final tenant mix.
projects.areaOrScale: Proposal-stage allowance: approximately 5,000–7,000 m² of retail and support floor area, predominantly one-storey pavilions with limited upper decks; indicative visitor capacity 800–1,200 people distributed across the public realm, subject to fire and crowd-flow review. Site allowance approximately 1.2–1.8 ha including covered lanes, rain court, service edge and landscape.
projects.structuralSystem: Use repetitive reinforced-concrete or steel-framed pavilion bays, provisionally 6–8 m, with laterite-clad non-loadbearing bases. The elevated canopy can be formed as a braced structural-steel or engineered aluminium truss/rib system spanning between designed supports at pavilion edges and selected independent columns; the perforated aluminium layer is secondary cladding, not the primary span structure. Provide movement joints between canopy and pavilion roofs, with foundations and lateral bracing designed for wind uplift and coastal exposure.
projects.constructionLogic: Build raised, flood-conscious site platforms and below-ground drainage before pavilion foundations, retaining accessible slopes and clear overland exceedance routes. Erect the canopy primary frame in engineered segments, brace it during erection, then install corrosion-protected secondary rails, perforated panels and the separate weathering roof layers. Repeated monitors need flashed curbs, insect screening, safe access and robust wind-driven-rain detailing; concealed gutters require maintainable outlets and emergency overflows. Waterproof and drain upper terraces independently, use slip-resistant paving with falls to trench drains or planted rain beds, and phase the open circulation network so tenant servicing can continue safely.
projects.environmentalResponse: Use the continuous canopy and deep verandas to shade shopfronts and public routes, while ventilated roof monitors exhaust accumulated hot air; preserve open sides and breezeways for cross-ventilation where wind-driven rain and comfort permit. Orient pavilion openings to capture prevailing breezes while shading east- and west-facing glazing with perforated screens. Raise occupied routes and critical electrical equipment above the locally established design flood level after site-specific assessment. Collect canopy runoff in accessible gutters for storage and reuse, and convey excess water to the planted rain court and designed site drainage system; use native coastal planting tolerant of wet seasons and salt-bearing air.

projects.functionalBrief: The proposed campus provides a low-rise workplace for teams that benefit from smaller neighborhood-scale office zones alongside shared meeting and staff amenities. Daily operations require direct, weather-protected connections among work pavilions, secure visitor reception, deliveries and facilities functions, with planted courts retained as useful circulation and respite spaces.
programme: Shared reception and visitor meeting rooms
Commons pavilion with café and multipurpose room
Covered verandas and planted rain gardens
projects.floorOrSiteOrganization: Arrange four low elongated parallel office pavilions around planted rain gardens and connect them with the single shared commons pavilion. A legible pedestrian spine links the arrival point, reception, commons and shaded verandas; work areas sit in the office bars, with meeting and support spaces close to the commons. Put service access, deliveries, waste and plant on a discrete perimeter edge, separated from the main pedestrian route. Provide accessible links between all pavilions and distribute protected exits so each occupied wing has short, direct egress to open air, subject to code review.
projects.areaOrScale: Proposal-stage campus allowance: approximately 7,000–9,000 m² gross internal area across predominantly one-storey pavilions, with an indicative regular workforce of 300–450 and visitor capacity based on separately scheduled commons events. Site allowance approximately 1.5–2.2 ha including pavilions, rain gardens, native trees, access and service circulation.
projects.structuralSystem: Use repetitive reinforced-concrete or structural-steel frames at roughly 6–8 m bays for the low pavilion bars, with masonry infill and lightweight roof construction. The broad shallow folded roof can use engineered steel trusses or rafters spanning pavilion widths, laterally braced and supported on regular columns; the commons may use a longer clear span subject to engineered truss design. Reinforced-concrete stair and service walls provide local stability where required; final foundations depend on geotechnical conditions.
projects.constructionLogic: Construct the pavilion frames and robust plinths first, then install roof trusses with temporary erection bracing before closing the roof with standing-seam weathering-steel panels over a drained, ventilated build-up. Detail deep eaves with continuous gutters, accessible downpipes, overflow scuppers and positive discharge to rain gardens; protect brickwork with damp-proof courses, cavity drainage and flashed openings. Fix dark perforated screens to secondary frames with corrosion-resistant fasteners and allow cleaning access to clerestories. Grade granite verandas away from walls, provide slip resistance and movement joints, and sequence planting after heavy equipment access is complete.
projects.environmentalResponse: Orient pavilion openings to enable cross-ventilation when outdoor humidity, noise and air quality permit, and use high clerestories for diffuse daylight without excessive glare. Broad roof overhangs, perforated screens and shaded verandas limit solar gain, while ceiling fans and efficient mixed-mode systems address humid periods. Preserve existing native trees where feasible and use rain gardens to detain and filter roof runoff, with overflow connections to approved site drainage. Choose locally suitable drought-tolerant planting for dry intervals and ensure planted areas have safe overflow, maintainable inlets and mosquito-conscious water management.

projects.functionalBrief: The proposed innovation centre supports flexible research, product development and collaboration in a compact workplace organized around a planted internal atrium. Staff need quiet project areas and shared laboratories or meeting rooms, while visitors require a clear reception route and building operations need secure servicing, robust vertical circulation and controlled access to technical areas.
programme: Flexible research and office work areas
IT, electrical, mechanical and storage rooms
projects.floorOrSiteOrganization: Organize a compact four-storey square ring of narrow perimeter floor plates around one planted rectangular atrium. Place the public entrance and reception at a shaded entry court, with visitor meeting rooms near the lobby; locate more secure research and work areas on upper levels with service rooms and vertical risers grouped at the core or secondary service nodes. Continuous galleries overlook the atrium but must not substitute for required protected escape routes; provide enclosed stairs and accessible lifts with direct, code-compliant discharge. Keep loading and plant access at the site edge, away from the entry court and primary pedestrian route.
projects.areaOrScale: Proposal-stage allowance: approximately 6,000–8,000 m² gross floor area over four levels, with an atrium footprint of roughly 350–500 m² and an indicative daily population of 250–400, subject to laboratory fit-out and occupancy review. Site allowance approximately 0.4–0.6 ha including entry court, service access and landscape.
projects.structuralSystem: A regular reinforced-concrete frame with an approximately 7.5–8.5 m grid and reinforced-concrete cores is appropriate for the four-storey ring; transfer beams around atrium edges should be minimized through aligned columns and consistent floor plates. The lightweight lattice atrium roof spans between designed perimeter supports using engineered aluminium or steel trusses, with uplift bracing and a clear ridge exhaust opening. Verify seismic, wind and thermal movement demands, and separate façade screen loads from the primary frame.
projects.constructionLogic: Build the concrete frame and atrium edge beams with temporary fall protection, then install the glazed and screened façade as a drained, replaceable rainscreen assembly. Terracotta fins and perforated champagne-metal screens attach to secondary brackets with allowance for differential movement and access for replacement; seal slab edges with tested fire-stopping. Assemble the lattice roof in manageable engineered sections, provide permanent bracing, weathering layers, screened high-level exhaust and a safe maintenance strategy. Waterproof the atrium base and planted areas with root barrier, protection and drainage layers; grade to accessible sumps or outlets, with emergency overflow independent of the occupied floors.
projects.environmentalResponse: The atrium provides a shaded internal landscape and diffuse daylight, while the lifted ridge opening can exhaust warm air by buoyancy when wind, rain and indoor conditions allow; provide controllable dampers or closures for storms and operational balancing. Terracotta fins, perforated outer screens and solar-control glazing should be tuned by orientation to reduce glare and cooling loads without making perimeter work areas dependent on artificial light. Deep galleries shade circulation and enable visual connection, with fans or mixed-mode conditioning as needed in humid weather. Capture roof water for appropriate reuse and landscape irrigation, provide a reliable overflow route, and use native drought-tolerant planting suited to the local climate.

projects.functionalBrief: The proposed mixed-use development combines active neighborhood retail with workplace and residential uses close to public transport. It must balance public passage and shop access at ground level with secure residential and office entrances, separate servicing, accessible vertical circulation and safe evacuation for distinct occupancies.
programme: Workplace floors and shared meeting rooms
Shared or separated parking and bicycle facilities
Planted terraces and resident amenity areas
projects.floorOrSiteOrganization: Place three offset mid-rise rectilinear blocks of varied heights on a continuous shaded retail plinth. A pedestrian passage cuts through the site from the transit-facing edge to the planted square; retail fronts this public route, while separate secure lobbies serve residential and workplace cores. Group loading, waste and plant at a discreet street edge with vehicle turning and timed deliveries, keeping it clear of the passage. Staggered upper levels create terraces and daylight gaps; provide independent protected stairs and accessible lifts for each occupancy/core, with final fire strategy, refuge and egress coordinated to local requirements.
projects.areaOrScale: Proposal-stage allowance: approximately 18,000–24,000 m² gross floor area across roughly 8–12 levels distributed among three blocks, including a retail plinth and upper mixed-use floors. Indicative programme of 4,000–6,000 m² retail, 7,000–9,000 m² workplace and 7,000–9,000 m² residential, subject to planning and unit mix; site allowance approximately 0.6–0.9 ha.
projects.structuralSystem: Use reinforced-concrete flat slabs or beam-and-slab framing on a regular 7.5–8.5 m grid, with separate reinforced-concrete cores providing lateral stability for each block. A continuous podium grid can support the retail plinth and align transfer zones; avoid extensive transfer structure by aligning upper columns with podium supports and resolving block offsets at clear structural joints. Design terrace edges and screens for wind loads, with foundations informed by geotechnical study and adjacent urban constraints.
projects.constructionLogic: Construct podium and cores with coordinated sleeves and risers, then repeat the upper floor frame using a consistent bay and prefabricated façade components where practical. Terracotta screen panels mount to engineered secondary rails with accessible fixings, drainage cavities and movement joints; recessed loggias receive continuous waterproofing turned up at doors, with threshold drainage and protected overflow. Detail planted terraces with root barrier, protection, drainage and irrigation isolation. Keep the public passage safely separated from construction and loading operations, provide temporary covered pedestrian routing where required, and coordinate podium fire separation and smoke control with the final mixed-use code strategy.
projects.environmentalResponse: The staggered block arrangement and passage preserve breezeways and daylight to the public realm, while stepped terraces provide planted shade without relying on broad exposed glazing. Recessed loggias, operable windows and red-brown terracotta screens temper direct sun; orient and tune screen density for the actual Pune site and prevailing winds. Use high-performance glazing selectively, with external shading on exposed orientations and mixed-mode ventilation only where noise, air quality and comfort permit. Harvest roof runoff for suitable reuse, direct podium drainage to maintainable systems, and provide native shade trees and planted terraces with controlled irrigation and safe overflow.

projects.functionalBrief: The proposed office tower provides flexible commercial floor plates for multiple tenants, supported by a public-facing lobby and shared building services. Its incremental floor rotation is treated as a restrained façade and perimeter expression around a stable, conventional core and frame; facilities, emergency response and façade maintenance remain practical and clearly planned.
programme: Loading, waste holding and facilities management
projects.floorOrSiteOrganization: Set a slender office tower on a street-scaled limestone podium with a planted forecourt. Locate reception, visitor waiting and shared amenities in the podium, with a clear lobby-to-lift sequence; place loading, waste, back-of-house and building plant at a screened service edge. Organize typical office floors around a regular central core with perimeter work zones, preserving stable core geometry while the façade and slab perimeter rotate by a small engineered increment between levels. Provide multiple protected stairs, fire-service access, accessible lifts and direct egress discharge designed to the applicable high-rise code.
projects.areaOrScale: Proposal-stage scale: approximately 24,000–32,000 m² gross floor area over 22–28 office levels above a two- to three-level podium, with typical plates of roughly 900–1,200 m² and an indicative total workplace population of 1,200–1,800 subject to final density and life-safety review. Urban site allowance approximately 0.4–0.7 ha including forecourt, drop-off and service access.
projects.structuralSystem: A reinforced-concrete central core provides primary lateral stability, paired with a regular reinforced-concrete flat-slab or beam-and-slab frame on an approximately 8–9 m office grid. Keep the core and column grid vertically aligned; achieve the subtle twist through controlled changes in perimeter slab edge and non-structural façade geometry rather than rotating major structural floors or creating unsupported cantilevers. Assess wind response, drift, seismic demand and foundation strategy through project-specific engineering.
projects.constructionLogic: Construct the core and repetitive floor frame using a coordinated climb sequence, with survey control at every level to set the modest perimeter offsets accurately. Install unitized curtain-wall panels in sequenced lifts with engineered slab-edge anchors, adjustable brackets and tested perimeter fire-stopping; accommodate floor-to-floor movement and maintain drainage at every rotated joint. Use podium limestone fins as mechanically anchored rainscreen elements over a drained cavity, with flashings and replaceable fixings. Provide a planned façade-maintenance system, safe roof access, and a continuous drainage strategy from crown to podium; coordinate tower crane, loading and public forecourt protection during construction.
projects.environmentalResponse: The slender floor plates should be oriented to balance daylight, views and solar exposure, with high-performance solar-control glazing and exterior shading calibrated to each façade orientation. The incremental rotation can vary exposure modestly but is not a substitute for engineered shading or energy analysis; use efficient lighting controls, well-zoned cooling and commissioning for multi-tenant operation. Provide shaded public forecourt planting and minimize heat-island surfaces, while collecting roof and podium runoff for suitable reuse and routing excess water to maintainable stormwater infrastructure. Operable windows are limited to locations where wind pressure, noise, air quality, security and the tower’s mechanical strategy make them viable.
